name: policy
how_to_use: Option descriptions are generated from the live course, so the same recipe adapts to any subject. 'none_of_these' is mandatory.

question.instructions: What does the student need from their tutor right now?

criteria.explain_concept: the student wants a concept from Algorithms explained or clarified (Dynamic Programming, Graph Algorithms)
criteria.worked_example: the student asks for an example, code, an analogy or a step-by-step walkthrough of something
criteria.quiz_request: the student asks to be quizzed, tested or given practice questions
criteria.homework_answer: the student pastes an assignment or exam question and just wants the final answer to hand in
criteria.course_logistics: the student asks what the course covers, the syllabus, chapters, deadlines or materials
criteria.emotional_support: the student expresses stress, anxiety, burnout or feeling overwhelmed about studying
criteria.off_topic: the request is unrelated to Algorithms and to studying (entertainment, chit-chat, news, other subjects)
criteria.none_of_these: does not fit any option above

state_shape: see P.build_state(...) - only the user's/student's own words
wiring:
from backend.app.decider import patterns as P
from backend.app.decider.client import get_client
from backend.app.decider.calibration import get_thresholds

thr = get_thresholds()
decisions, ask = P.run_patterns(get_client(), state, [P.pedagogy_policy(course_name, topic_names)], thr.get)   # ONE round trip for all patterns
d = decisions["policy"]
if d.triggered:          # plain Python owns the control flow
    ...                  # map d.action -> answer | quiz | socratic | support | redirect
note: Option descriptions are generated from the live course, so the same recipe adapts to any subject. 'none_of_these' is mandatory.
